details:
WHAT IT DOES AND HOW IT WORKS
Red Horizon is a browser-based survival game that teaches how a Mars outpost really runs. After a crash landing leaves the ship damaged and cut off from Earth, players build the outpost. They place solar arrays, water and ore extractors, a workshop, and a greenhouse, while keeping power, oxygen, water, and food in balance. Once the Radar and Mission Control Uplink restore contact, Earth warns that a dust storm is coming. Players must then extract a geological sample, activate a beacon, and request evacuation before the deadline.

The game turns real mission constraints into gameplay. Machines draw power, carry radiation exposure, and cost materials and time, so no choice is free. Failures end in a clear Mission Failed screen that shows what went wrong, such as power running out and oxygen dropping.

It matters because it lets players experience the trade-offs astronauts and mission planners face every day. They build intuition for engineering under pressure through play.

BENEFITS
Players learn by doing instead of reading. Every machine draws power and has radiation exposure, materials are limited, and time is limited, so no choice is free. Failing is safe: the game shows why the mission failed and lets the player load a save or start again. Short guided tasks and clear on-screen numbers keep it approachable for players.

INTENDED IMPACT
We want a player to walk away understanding that survival in deep space is a budgeting problem. Power, oxygen, materials, and time are all limited, and good engineering means choosing under pressure. We hope it sparks interest in space engineering and gives everyone a playful way to introduce those ideas.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY
Languages and framework: Typescript, React.js, Tailwind CSS
Rendering and game engine: Phaser.js
Hosting and platform: Vercel

CREATIVITY
The story twist is the core idea. Players think they are building a permanent home on Mars. Only after reconnecting with Earth do they learn that the real mission is a race against a storm. That turns a building game into a decision game halfway through. Mission Control messages, an Earth-online uplink screen, and a rescue-readiness checklist make the player feel part of a real mission.

FACTORS WE CONSIDERED
- Fairness: every module costs power, time, or materials, so no choice is free.
- Pacing: speed controls and a guided task list keep players moving through the mission.
- Scope: we focused on one complete mission loop that works end to end.
